To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the intrinsic apoptosis pathway is a promising target for the development of new glioma therapies, (ii) pro-apoptotic and pro-autophagic agents are able to induce glioma cell death in vitro and in vivo, (iii) the combination of pro-apoptotic with pro-autophagic compounds may be more efficient in killing glioma cells than single agents,
the induction of caspase- and caspase-independent apoptosis and autophagic cell-death are promising therapeutic approaches in GBM.
the combination of apoptosis and autophysic induction is a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of glioma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of new molecular targets and their therapeutic potential in GBM.

the identification of novel molecular targets for glioma therapy, the development of novel molecularly targeted therapies, the identification of predictive markers of response to these novel therapies and the development of novel imaging techniques to monitor response to treatment in vivo.
the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of GBMs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is still a long way to go before apoptosis and autophagic drugs can be considered for the treatment of GBMs.
the therapeutic potential of apoptosis and autopahy-based therapies is not yet fully exploited in glioma.
the combination of pro-apoptotic and pro-autophagic agents might be a promising therapeutic strategy to improve current GBM therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the induction of autophagy and apoptosis in glioblastoma cells by pro-apoptotic and pro-autophagic therapies may be a novel and promising approach to treat glioma patients.
we have identified a novel pro-apoptotic mechanism that is mediated by the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) and that is independent of the BCL-2 proteins.
apoptosis is the most important pathway to induce cell death in glioma cells, while autophagy seems to have a tumor-protective function and may serve as a survival mechanism for glioma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the therapeutic exploitation of apoptosis and/or autophagy is a promising approach to treat glioma.
a combination of drugs that target both the extrinsic and intrinsic apoptotic pathway as well as autophagic cell killing may represent a more promising therapeutic approach for GBM patients.
the therapeutic exploitation of apoptosis and/or autophagy for GBMs is a very promising approach.
